metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly; reduce forecast slope after peak and introduce mean reversion trigger at 2–3 standard deviations above mean.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize the turning point; add lagged correction rule: if 3 consecutive days of true price < 10% below prior peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overreacts to short-term noise; use sentiment history as a proxy for market direction — if sentiment remains neutral, forecast should be anchored to historical mean, not trend.
